Jonas / Ben —

Draft response outline below. I kept commercial language tight so legal can paste it into their template. Please flag anything that is not safe to promise to an enterprise procurement timeline (~2 weeks).

Proposed commitments to send to Alto Health:
1) Region anchoring: For accounts choosing EU anchoring (paid add-on), Redwood will ensure primary inference processing and persistent storage of customer data remain within the EU region. We provide a contractual Region Anchoring SLA of 99.9% regional-processing uptime measured per calendar month. Temporary cross-region failover is allowed for operational necessity only and is constrained to a maximum of 72 consecutive hours in any 90-day rolling window unless mutually agreed in writing. Events and failovers will be logged and notified per the Incident Notification schedule.

2) KMS handshake & key custody: For Private or Dedicated customers, keys remain customer-managed where requested. For hosted EU-anchored accounts using Redwood-managed KMS, Redwood will:
- Maintain keys in an EU-backed KMS pool.
- In emergency cross-region failover, keys are not exported; instead a temporary, tightly-scoped decryption session is authorized via an auditable KMS grant/role for the minimum window required.
- All KMS grants, rotations, and transient decryption activities will be recorded in our audit trail (UTC timestamps) and provided as CSV extracts on request for SOC review.

Attachments to send: DPA redline response (PDF) and a KMS escrow/rotation schedule template (XLSX).

Ben — can you confirm the technical feasibility and whether we should change the 72h window wording? Also, any telemetry example we can safely surface (redacted) for the audit snippet?

Thanks — M

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Claire / Katie —

Thanks for the patience. From an infra/security standpoint the proposed language is acceptable with two clarifications I added below so we don't overpromise operational mechanics:

1) 72h temporary failover: Confirmed as a contractual cap for hosted EU-anchored customers. Operationally, any failover is subject to root-cause constraints (e.g., global hardware outage vs routine maintenance). We'll include an explicit "failure reason" taxonomy in the MOP (runbook) so Alto can reconcile why a window was used.

2) KMS behavior in failover: We will not export customer keys. For Redwood-managed keys the failover path uses short-lived KMS grants with precise scope (decrypt: inference-session) and TTLs tied to the failover duration. We can provide an audit excerpt: one line per grant with fields [timestamp_utc, grant_id, scope, actor_id, duration_seconds, reason_code]. Example (redacted):
2026-04-02T03:12:23Z, GRANT-6a4f, decrypt:inference-session, infra-runner-12, 259200, FAILOVER_NETWORK_OUTAGE

3) Evidence delivery: We can supply CSV extracts and a time-bound KMS rotation schedule (xlsx) as part of the onboarding pack. For Private deployments (customer-managed KMS) we will provide a handshake checklist and verification steps rather than access to keys.

Next steps: Jonas / Marissa to send the refined DPA response and the two attachments. I'll add the sample CSV line to the attachment and highlight the rotation cadence.

Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
